details: Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf announced on October 4, 2026, that the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until the United States fulfills seven conditions outlined in the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding. These conditions reportedly include the lifting of economic sanctions and a complete cessation of hostilities. This declaration follows a series of recent tanker attacks in the region and signifies escalating tensions between the US and Iran. A prolonged closure of this critical waterway could disrupt global oil supplies, increase shipping costs, and potentially lead to inflationary pressures.
title: Iran: Strait of Hormuz Stays Shut Amid US Demands

details: On October 1, 2026, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) unveiled proposed new rules and amendments to establish a clearer regulatory framework for how registered investment advisers and regulated funds can custody crypto assets. SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins stated that this initiative aims to provide a compliant pathway where regulatory uncertainty previously existed, modernizing existing custody rules. The proposal allows for self-custody in limited circumstances and permits state trust companies to act as custodians, potentially expanding avenues for institutional participation in crypto markets.
title: SEC Proposes Clearer Crypto Custody Rules for Investment Advisers
